newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees tight oils, oilmeals stocks.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees tight oils, oilmeals stocks.

text.p: World oilmeal stocks on March 31, 1997 were estimated at 4.9 million tonnes, down 18 percent from a year earlier and the lowest figure in seven years, the independent newsletter Oil World said.
The lower figure would result from a high rate of consumption in Oct/March 1996/97, especially of soymeal.
Total meal consumption in these six months was pegged at 87.0 million tonnes, exceeding output by 2.1 million tonnes.
The figures applied to the 12 most important oilmeals.
The supply situation in oils and fats was more relaxed as higher carry-in stocks of palm, soy, sun and rape oil had helped boost Oct 1, 1996 stocks of 17 key oils and fats.
They were at 12.2 million tonnes, seven percent more than a year earlier.

But strong demand growth was bound to reduce these stocks to 11.5 million tonnes by the end of March, five percent below the level 12 months earlier, and to 10.9 million at end-September, down from 12.2 million previously.
Global seed oil output would fall short of demand in April/September 1997 despite higher output of palm, olive and corn oils and animal fats, Oil World said.
